messages:
Maya: Thanks for the talk today. Two quick pricing/usage follow-ups people keep asking about: (1) how do temporary promo credits interact with rate limits and (2) what happens if free-trial customers spike on embeddings?

Josh: Good q. Promo credits are only a currency offset; they do not change rate limits. So you can have promo balance but still be 429d'ed if you hit the RPS/parallel-request limits. We'll add a short FAQ entry.

Renee: For embeddings spikes: free-trial accounts get a small shared burst pool for the first 48h to smooth onboarding. After that, normal per-key limits apply. Overages beyond free trial burst are billed if they exceed credits.

Maya: Can we add an example "math" for teams to understand when they'll be billed? People want a simple calc.

Josh: Example: if model costs $0.0004 / token and you run a 1k-token embedding job for 1000 items that's 1M tokens = $400. If you have a promo credit of $200 it covers half, the rest is billed. Rate limits can still reject the job if you submit concurrently above the allowed parallelism.

Vik: Ops note: we enforce three types of limits: per-key QPS (requests/sec), per-route concurrent calls, and token-rate smoothing. We allow short micro-bursts (token burst window ~3-10s depending on plan) but sustained high throughput requires commit/dedicated capacity.

Maya: Where do customers see their remaining promo credit quickly?

billing-bot: Customers can see balances in Console > Billing > Credits. API header also includes X-Credit-Balance and billing-explanation link: https://console.redwood/billing/docs/credits.

Renee: Also adding a note: credit "top-ups" via support are possible for trials (manual), and account teams can authorize temporary larger burst pools for enterprise pilots.

Josh: Roadmap snippet: we're working on an auto-top-up mechanism (opt-in) and a per-route throughput SLA product. ETA: prototyping next quarter.

Maya: One last clarification: fallback to smaller/cheaper models during regional pressure  how is that billed and how is it communicated?

Vik: Billing is for the model that served the request. We surface fallback events in the console timeline and expose a per-request header X-Model-Served. We record metrics so you can reconcile cost/downgrade events. Customers can opt-out of automatic fallback in route settings.

infra-bot: Pinned document: /handbook/ops/rate-limits-and-burst-policy.md (internal).

Maya: Perfect. Can someone draft a 2-line blurb for support to paste into replies when customers see 429 but have credits?

Josh: Draft blurb: "429 indicates your request rate exceeded the account's configured throughput. Credits cover cost but do not increase request-rate capacity. Check X-RateLimit-* headers and, if needed, request a rate-cap review or dedicated capacity via sales."

Renee: I'll add that to the support canned responses.

Maya: Great, thanks. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
